clue.text: Gent with ulcer, a tormented member of the family

indicators.note: something tormented is twisted and racked, so these letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A gentleman with a stomach ulcer is one suffering relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is just a joining word; GENT, ULCER and A together are rearranged, signalled by 'tormented'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's uncle is a relative, so he is one member of the family tree.

clue.text: Escargot? One has good parts for munching!

indicators.note: munching chews things up, so these letters are chewed into a new order

explanation.surface: A snail dish has tasty bits worth chewing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One has' is a link. The question mark shows the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An escargot is an edible snail, and snails are members of the mollusc class of slugs and snails.

clue.text: Poem set down within English words on stage

indicators.note: the record word sits inside the theatre word

parts.note: a cue is the line that signals an actor's next speech
to log is to record in writing

explanation.surface: Verse written into English dialogue for the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, as in Virgil's Eclogues.

clue.text: Better prepared for battle, being angry

explanation.surface: More ready for a fight because one is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both literally armed and figuratively roused to protest.

clue.text: Co-stars making a nightly appearance

parts.note: a pair of stars sharing billing who show up every night, read as twin stars in the sky

explanation.surface: Two leading actors performing in a show every night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Co-stars' suggests actors in a long-running show; it means two actual stars, the brightest in Gemini.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the twin brothers of myth, and the two bright stars of the Gemini constellation.

clue.text: Pretentious handful almost upset social event

indicators.note: upset in a down clue tips the shortened word over, reading it backwards
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a handful means a small number, a few
a fete is an outdoor fundraising fair

explanation.surface: A small crowd at a showy party nearly overturned it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims FEW to FE; 'upset' turns that to EF. A fete is a British village or church fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete describes affected, over-refined people, close in sense to pretentious.

clue.text: Old man, someone revered in history

parts.note: an informal word for one's father is pa
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a person revered for holiness

explanation.surface: A father or a venerated figure from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lies in history is gone by, a straight synonym for over and done.

clue.text: Servant admitting crime in minister's house

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a page is a young attendant or servant
arson is the crime of setting fire to property

explanation.surface: A servant confesses to an offence in a clergyman's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' looks like confessing, but it means letting in.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is the residence provided for a parish clergyman.

clue.text: Small son parent's given blanket

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, here a small or shortened son
a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: A little boy's mum hands over a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link. 'blanket' is a verb here, to cover thickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to cover it completely, as snow can blanket a field.

clue.text: A desperate appeal to provide cover for legal requests

indicators.note: the distress call is wrapped around the other piece, covering it on both sides

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: A frantic plea that might shield someone's legitimate demands.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask for or seek something, so it is a verb synonym for requests.

clue.text: Litter in distant part of allotment maybe

parts.note: far means a long way off
vegetables on an allotment plot are planted in rows

explanation.surface: Rubbish dumped at the far end of a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented patch of ground in Britain for growing vegetables. 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrow is a litter of piglets born to a sow at one time.

clue.text: Equipment needed by a capital city

parts.note: a rig is apparatus or gear, as in a drilling rig

explanation.surface: A capital needs its gear and kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital of Latvia, so it is an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Mark's rhetorical digression

definitions.meaning: a punctuation sign used for possession or omitted letters
a turn in a speech to address someone absent or an abstraction directly

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark goes off on a speechifying tangent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions; 'Mark' looks like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the punctuation sign and the orator's device of breaking off to address someone absent.

clue.text: Report of truce spread by degrees

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a truce is peace, and a spread is a meal laid out, giving a peace meal

explanation.surface: News of a ceasefire filters out gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means bit by bit, in stages, a synonym for gradually or by degrees.

clue.text: Conservative rural community often heard of in the city

parts.note: Ambridge is the fictional village in The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap

explanation.surface: A Tory village that city folk often hear about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' hints the village is from radio, not a homophone; The Archers is a BBC Radio 4 farming soap. 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is an English university city.

clue.text: Shakespeare, one admitted to be an inventive man

indicators.note: one piece is let in inside the other

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard of Avon
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Shakespeare, a single man who must be acknowledged as creative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link. John Logie Baird was the Scottish engineer who demonstrated early television.
explanation.definitionFit: Baird invented an early television system, so he is a real inventor.

clue.text: Mother wants a setting for ornament

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a scene is the place where action is set

explanation.surface: A mother needs a backdrop for decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' and 'for' are links. 'ornament' is a verb: to decorate metal with inlaid patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: To damascene is to decorate metal with inlaid gold or silver, so to ornament it.

clue.text: Where American detected electricity very quickly

parts.note: in answers the question where, telling the location
a flash is a sudden burst of electricity, as lightning

explanation.surface: Where an American stumbled upon electrical power at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detected' is a link between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means instantly, as quick as a lightning spark.

clue.text: Mum backing up rogue's principles

indicators.note: the mother word supports from behind, so it comes after the other piece

parts.note: dog is an old word for a scoundrel or rogue
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother supports a scoundrel's beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing up' looks like a reversal signal, but nothing turns round: here it means supporting from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of firmly held tenets, so it fits principles collectively.

clue.text: Not allowing passage through a large town after work

indicators.note: the town part comes after the work part

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A big town after the job doesn't let you through.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the quality, so 'Not allowing passage through' stands for the noun: the state of letting no light through.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is the property of blocking light, the condition of letting nothing pass through.

clue.text: A rumpus before school period gets one kept in for a while

parts.note: a din is a loud uproar

indicators.note: like a pupil in detention, the letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: a school year is split into terms
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A row before term leads to a pupil's detention for some time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' and 'gets' are links. The Latin phrase means in the meantime.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means temporarily, in the meantime, equal to for a while.

clue.text: Island gathering of the clans

definitions.meaning: a French island in the Indian Ocean near Mauritius
a meeting of family or old friends coming together again

explanation.surface: A Scottish clan meet held on an isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Réunion is an Indian Ocean island, and a reunion is a gathering of people who meet again.

clue.text: Secure unusual cactus

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are set out differently

explanation.surface: A rare cactus kept safely.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereus is a genus of tall columnar cacti, some night-flowering.

clue.text: Managed to be removed on a stretcher?

definitions.meaning: succeeded in doing something, as in pulled it off
literally borne away, as an injured player is

explanation.surface: Someone coped well, and then was taken off injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' joins the two senses; the question mark marks the literal one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both succeeded at something and literally borne away by others.

clue.text: Kiss a maiden lady immune to Cupid's darts

definitions.meaning: an old word for a smacking kiss

definitions.text: a maiden lady immune to Cupid's darts
definitions.meaning: Frances ..., Victorian headmistress, mocked in the rhyme 'Miss ... and Miss Beale, Cupid's darts do not feel'

explanation.surface: A peck for a spinster who never falls in love.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense relies on a Victorian rhyme about two pioneering, unmarried headmistresses of girls' schools.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a kiss, and the surname of the famous unmarried Victorian headmistress.

clue.text: Run through unsolved problem

definitions.meaning: to pierce with many holes, as with bullets
a puzzle or mystery yet to be explained

explanation.surface: Going over a mystery that remains unanswered.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle is to perforate, and a riddle is an enigma, two separate senses.

clue.text: Detail troubled me in interval before production

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A fine point worried me during the wait before manufacture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges only the first word; 'me' stays as written at the end, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the time between ordering or starting something and its being produced.

clue.text: Pretty person innately able to become a model

indicators.note: innately means within, so the answer lies inside the words

explanation.surface: An attractive person naturally suited to modelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'able to become a' links the hidden word to its definition; 'model' looks like a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a representative example or pattern, a sense shared with model.

clue.text: Faculty without an obvious reception area?

definitions.text: Faculty without an obvious reception area?

parts.words: Faculty without an obvious reception area?
parts.note: a faculty is a power of the mind; this one receives impressions with no organ like eye or ear to receive them

explanation.surface: A university department with no visible front desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' suggests a college department and 'reception area' an office foyer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an intuitive power of perception beyond sight, hearing, touch, taste and smell.
